Subject: DPA Qs: deletion windows, backups & onshore restore

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft DPA — attached are a few questions the security/legal team asked while we review. Can you confirm the following so we can sign off?

1) Delete semantics: when you say "delete" in the DPA, does that include immutable backups and snapshots? If so, what's the practical window for backups to be purged after a customer-initiated erasure request?

2) Onshore/geo fallback: we need a written commitment that customer data for "Aurum Health" will not be restored from an offshore backup without our explicit approval. If you use cross-region replication for resilience, what controls do you offer to prevent cross-border restores?

3) Certification of erasure: can Redwood provide a certificate of deletion (signed statement) once the erasure process completes? If not, what logs/evidence do you provide and what retention do those logs have?

4) Legal hold carveouts: please explain your process to hold data for litigation while still complying with the deletion SLA — how do you isolate held records, and what timeframes apply to removing held status?

Attached: Aurum_DPA_questions_20280214.pdf (list of prioritized items). We are aiming to finalize the DPA by the end of next week.

Best,

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then Connor (legal) and Monica (platform) are looped to provide the precise language we can accept in the DPA.

Summary answers:
- "Delete" in the DPA: production data is removed from live serving layers within 24 hours of an accepted erasure request. Backups/snapshots: we typically run a scheduled backup/retention cycle and propose they be purged within 90 days of the deletion request, except where retained for lawful hold.
- Geo/restore: we can commit that customer-initiated restores to a region outside the contracted geolocation require a documented approval flow (recorded request + approval by customer security contact). Cross-region automated restores are not performed for customer data without explicit authorization.
- Certificate of deletion: we can provide a signed deletion certificate and supporting purge logs for the retention/backup lifecycle (we'll propose a standard format).
- Legal hold: we support tagging records as "legal hold"; held records will be excluded from purge pipelines until hold release. We can propose language that specifies the hold process and an escalation flow for time-boxed holds.

I've attached our starting redline so you can see proposed text. Connor — can you add legal redlines for the backup/snapshot and certificate sections? Monica — can you confirm the operational purge windows and what evidence we can provide (logs, snapshot manifests)?

Next step: Connor will send a redline; once agreed we can schedule a short call to close the last open points.

Thanks,

Hi all — attaching a legal redline with proposed language (Redwood_DPA_redline_kco.docx). Key points from our side and suggested wording:

1) Backup retention window (proposed clause): "For clarity, 'Deletion' shall mean removal from the primary production environment within 24 hours of acceptance. Backups, snapshots and archival copies will be purged in the ordinary course of business and, absent a lawful hold, within ninety (90) calendar days of the Deletion request being accepted by Redwood. Where technical constraints prevent immediate purge of immutable snapshots, Redwood will render the data cryptographically inaccessible (e.g., encryption key destruction) and record the action in the purge log."

2) Geo-restore controls (proposed clause): "Redwood will not perform a cross-border restore of Customer Data to any location not previously agreed in writing by the Customer. Any restore to a non-contracted geography requires a documented approval from an authorized Customer security contact and will be fully audited."

3) Certificate of deletion (proposed clause): "Upon completion of the purge process, Redwood will provide Customer with a Certificate of Deletion that includes (i) timestamp of purge completion, (ii) list of purged resource identifiers, and (iii) hash of the purge manifest. Redwood will retain the purge logs for a period of one (1) year after purge completion for audit purposes unless otherwise agreed."

4) Legal hold process (proposed clause): "Customer may place a Data Subject or subset of Customer Data on lawful hold by submitting a written request to Redwood. Data under lawful hold shall be excluded from purge cycles until Customer provides written release. Redwood may require up to seven (7) business days to implement a hold in live systems; where holds involve archived media, an implementation estimate will be provided."

Open items for negotiation:
- Whether the backup purge window should be 90 or 180 days for healthcare customers with stringent audit needs (we can offer 90 by default and 180 as a negotiated option with a small surcharge).
- Retention of purge logs: we propose 1 year; customer requested certification might want longer.

Elena — if you can flag redlines you'd accept vs. those you'd like changed, we can incorporate and move to sign-off.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
